# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the display, light, and wire contents are all unknown to me. I need the Mute to read the manual and obtain the Deaf’s visual report, then relay both to me before I cut anything. I am asking for the exact required condition and all visible markings, especially which wire is safe or required.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and report its exact required action. Also obtain the Deaf's complete report of the display, light, and all wire markings, then relay everything to me. I will not cut a wire until you do.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb display is 0. Light is blue. Wires from left to right are blue, green, yellow. Mute signalled: index-up, I-love-you, OK, victory, raised palm, OK, I-love-you, open hand.

The Deaf has provided the visual facts: display 0, blue light, and wires blue, green, yellow. The Mute’s gestures may contain the manual’s instruction, but I cannot perceive gestures, so I still do not know which wire to cut. I am asking the Mute to communicate the manual’s result through the Deaf, who can then speak it aloud.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot perceive your gestures. Please use your gesture code to tell the Deaf the manual's required wire and have the Deaf say that wire aloud on the next turn.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: pointing at you, pointing right, pointing down, pointing up, I-love-you hand, OK hand, victory sign, raised palm, OK hand, I-love-you hand, raised palm, thumbs down. Bomb display 0, light yellow, wires blue green yellow.

The bomb facts are now confirmed as display 0, yellow light, and wires blue, green, yellow. However, the Deaf’s description of the Mute’s gestures does not give me a reliable wire number; I must not guess from an unknown gesture code. I am asking the Mute to send only the required wire number using an explicit one-, two-, or three-finger convention, which the Deaf can report unambiguously.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture only the required wire number: use ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3, with no other gestures. Deaf, please report that single gesture to me in words.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: raised palm, then pointing left. Current bomb view: display 0, light red, wires blue green yellow.

I still do not have a trustworthy wire choice. The latest two gestures—raised palm followed by pointing left—could mean an instruction such as “stop, left,” but that is not an established code and guessing would detonate the bomb. I am defining a simple unambiguous code now: one pointing gesture only, with left = wire 1, down = wire 2, and right = wire 3.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Send exactly one gesture for the wire to cut: point left means wire 1, point down means wire 2, and point right means wire 3. Do not add any other gesture. Deaf, report that one gesture exactly.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: pointing up. Current bomb view: display 0, light white, wires blue green yellow.

The latest signal is pointing up, which is outside the wire code I specified, so it does not identify a wire safely. The bomb’s current visible state is display 0, white light, and wires blue, green, yellow, but I still lack the manual’s actual rule. I am requesting an explicit spoken wire number from the Mute, which avoids any gesture ambiguity.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the required wire number plainly: say exactly wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3. Do not use gestures for this answer.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: pointing left. Current bomb view: display 0, light green, wires blue green yellow.

The Mute has now sent exactly one gesture, pointing left, matching the unambiguous convention I requested for wire 1. The Deaf confirms the current state is display 0, green light, and wires blue, green, yellow. I will therefore cut wire 1.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
